To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the vertical structure of natural and built environments in top-of-canopy LiDAR-derived surface models significantly alters the scale, complexity, and naturalness of viewscapes compared with bare-earth surface models.
LiDAR-derived top-of-canopy models produce more realistic viewscapes compared with models based on bare earth surface data.

(1) LiDAR-derived top-of-canopy models produced significantly smaller, more private, and more realistic viewscapes than LiDAR-derived bare-earth models; (2) LiDAR models of varying resolutions produced increasingly exaggerated viewscape sizes and shapes; and (3) LiDAR-based viewscapes can be used to assess the scale and complexity of viewscapes in exurban areas, and can be applied to other landscape and urban planning contexts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the visual impact of exurban development on natural landscapes.
how to better model and understand the 3-D structure of exurban viewscopes.
the effects of exurban development on the quality of viewscapes in a region of rapidly growing low-density housing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of LiDAR ToC models is recommended for exurban viewscaping applications.
the vertical dimension of the environment should be considered in viewscapes.
ToC models are better at representing the actual viewscapes experienced by residents, and that BE models overestimate the size and quality (e.g., greenness and diversity) of viewscapes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the vertical structure of vegetation is an important factor in determining the scale and quality of viewscape for residents of exurban areas.
we found that the top-of-canopy viewscapes of homes in exurban landscapes are much smaller than those derived from bare-earth models.

the use of bare earth LiDAR models to study viewscape characteristics in urbanizing landscapes can lead to overestimation of the amount of greenness and underestimation of ruggedness and private viewscape size.
The main takeaway from our work is that

viewscapes are not just about the horizontal extent of a viewshed, but also about the vertical structure of the landscape and how it affects the scale, complexity, and naturalness of the surrounding environment.

viewscapes derived solely from BE models can overestimate the amount of natural vegetation in viewscapes, underestimate the ruggedness of surrounding landscape features, and underestimate the number of neighbors seen in viewscapes.
LiDAR data can be used to model realistic, comprehensive viewscape metrics that account for 3-D elements that are not visible in bare-earth digital elevation model data.
